_readme: The crew: you are the Senior Astronaut (Commander). Each Junior Astronaut has a specialty: on tasks in their specialty they work faster and get a bigger result. Each Junior can finish one task per sol. 'inside' tasks happen in the habitat.

tasks.label: Tend the greenhouse
tasks.start: Copy that, Commander. Heading to the greenhouse.
tasks.done: Plants watered, roots checked, LEDs cleaned. They look healthy!
tasks.fact: On the ISS, astronauts water plants by hand with a syringe because water doesn't flow downward in microgravity. On the Moon and Mars, gravity helps a little.

tasks.label: Pile regolith on the hab
tasks.start: On it. Grabbing the shovel to add regolith to the shield.
tasks.done: Another layer of regolith is on the roof. That cuts our radiation dose.
tasks.fact: About 1–2 metres of regolith over a habitat blocks most solar particles and a good share of cosmic rays. Real bases will use robots, but here we dig by hand.

tasks.label: Clean the solar panels
tasks.start: Copy. Heading out to brush dust off the panels.
tasks.done: Panels are clean. We're making a little more power now.
tasks.fact: Dust on solar panels was a real problem for Mars rovers. Spirit and Opportunity were sometimes saved by 'cleaning events' when gusts of wind blew their panels clean.

tasks.label: Repair life support
tasks.start: Copy that. Grabbing the toolkit and heading to the life-support rack.
tasks.fact: ISS crews spend hours every week on maintenance. The oxygen generator and water recycler are checked and repaired regularly.

tasks.label: Collect rock samples
tasks.start: Heading to the rock field with sample bags.
tasks.done: Samples bagged and labelled for the lab.
tasks.fact: Astronauts collected 382 kg of Moon rock during the Apollo missions. Scientists are still studying them today.

tasks.label: Analyse samples in the lab
tasks.start: Going inside to run the samples through the lab instruments.
tasks.done: Analysis complete. Data sent to Earth.
tasks.fact: Perseverance carries instruments like PIXL and SHERLOC that can map the chemistry of a rock in spots smaller than a grain of salt.

tasks.label: Rest in the sleep pod
tasks.start: Thanks, Commander. Heading inside for a rest.
tasks.fact: Sleep is hard in space: astronauts on the ISS sleep in sleeping bags strapped to the wall and use eye masks because the Sun rises 16 times a day.

tasks.label: Inspect the reactor
tasks.start: Heading out to the reactor. I'll stay behind the berm.
tasks.fact: The reactor sits far from the habitat behind a regolith berm. Distance and shielding are the two best ways to stay safe from radiation.

meal.text: The crew shares a hot meal in the galley. Eating together keeps morale up on long missions.
